anomalies.description: A man walks toward a red plastic chair and deliberately kicks it, causing it to tip over and slide across the pavement — this constitutes vandalism (damaging street furniture where it stands).

original_descriptions.description: A man walks toward a red plastic chair and deliberately kicks it, causing it to tip over and slide across the pavement — this constitutes vandalism (damaging street furniture where it stands).

A man in a dark shirt approaches a yellow object (likely a vending machine or utility box) near the storefront and repeatedly strikes or kicks it with force over several seconds, consistent with vandalism—damaging property where it stands. The action is deliberate, sustained, and not typical of normal interaction.

A person in dark clothing is seen approaching a parked white car with its driver-side door open, then appears to strike or forcefully interact with the vehicle near the open door (frames 1–3), before quickly walking away (frames 4–6). The motion suggests possible vandalism—such as smashing a window or damaging the door—consistent with the defined anomaly type of damaging property where it stands. No other individuals intervene, and the action is abrupt and non-routine.
